workLog.action: Measured the two-dot versus three-dot diff on a branch 7 commits behind main
workLog.result: origin/main..HEAD reported 62 files, 207 insertions and 4978 deletions for a change that adds three lines and deletes nothing. origin/main...HEAD and an explicit merge-base diff both reported 4 files, 118 insertions, 0 deletions. The existing memory already told readers to use the three-dot form but never said what the two-dot form does, which is the half that causes the wrong decision.

workLog.action: Diagnosed an opaque 'Session End validation failed' from new_pr.py
workLog.result: The gate diffs against the local main ref, which was 44 commits behind. That surfaced 19 session logs as changed, and the gate validates only the highest-numbered one, which was 2026-08-02-session-4231-episode-corpus-migration.json, a file this branch never touched. Its endingCommit is legitimately not an ancestor of this HEAD. The branch's own log passed standalone in the same worktree under the same interpreter, which is what ruled out every other cause. git fetch origin main:main fast-forwarded the ref and the PR created on the next attempt.

workLog.action: Checked the fix was safe before moving the ref
workLog.result: git rev-list --left-right --count main...origin/main reported 0 ahead and 44 behind, and git worktree list showed the primary clone on a detached HEAD, so main was checked out nowhere and the fast-forward could not discard work or disturb another worktree.

workLog.action: Chose the persistence surface for each finding rather than defaulting to a new memory file
workLog.result: The git finding extends the memory that already owns diff-count lies, keeping one source of truth. The gate finding went to GOTCHAS.md beside the existing endingCommit entry, because the two share a symptom string and differ in cause, so a reader who lands on the existing entry alone will hunt for an amend they never made.
